Question: Q1
Notes: Interpretation: the expert consensus names only 'Occupation' with no mechanism specified — the IG realises it as three coded axes rather than a free-text job title, which carries little analytical value: employment status (LOINC 67875-5, official answer list LL1901-9 plus one local 'self-employed' addition that list is missing, verified July 2026), occupational physical-demand intensity (fully local — sedentary/light-manual/heavy-manual; no SNOMED/LOINC concept exists, verified July 2026), and occupational overhead-work exposure (fully local yes/no/unknown; no SNOMED/LOINC concept exists, verified July 2026). Overhead exposure is an axis independent of physical-demand intensity, so an occupation that is simultaneously heavy AND overhead (e.g. a roofer) is not forced into an either/or choice. Physical demand/overhead exposure are novel axes not captured by any comparable registry (DART/EPRD/IRD/SEPR), directly motivated by overhead/repetitive shoulder loading being a well-established rotator-cuff risk and return-to-work factor. See ADR-0082, ADR-0105.
IG Implementation: EmploymentStatusObservation profile (code = LOINC#67875-5; valueCodeableConcept required-bound to hybrid EmploymentStatus ValueSet) + OccupationalPhysicalDemandObservation profile (code = ShoulderObservationCodes#occupational-physical-demand; valueCodeableConcept required-bound to local OccupationalPhysicalDemand ValueSet, 3 intensity tiers) + OccupationalOverheadExposureObservation profile (code = ShoulderObservationCodes#occupational-overhead-exposure; valueCodeableConcept required-bound to local OccupationalOverheadExposure ValueSet).

Question: Q1
Notes: expert consensus Q1.l "workmen's compensation" is one of 13 patient-history factors in the Q1 unanimous-consensus list; the expert consensus names it as a single yes/no clinical flag with no further decomposition. The IG realises a "yes" answer as a ShoulderCoverage with Coverage.type = v3-ActCode#WCBPOL (worker's compensation, German Berufsgenossenschaft); "no"/"unknown" answers emit no Coverage resource. The clinical/medicolegal rationale is well-established: WC status implies a work-related injury (Arbeitsunfall), triggers a different documentation pathway (Durchgangsarzt-Verfahren), and is a known outcome confounder in shoulder literature. Broader payer categorisation (GKV/PKV/Selbstzahler) is intentionally out of scope — not named by the expert consensus, and the v3-ActCode coverage of German payer types is partial anyway (no exact PKV code; HL7 DE Basisprofil deferred). See ADR-0061.
IG Implementation: ShoulderCoverage profile (Parent: Coverage; type 1..1 extensible-bound to coverage-type, fixed in practice to v3-ActCode#WCBPOL by the form). StepPatient.tsx 'Workers' Compensation' yes/no/unknown field emits Coverage entry into RotatorCuffRegistrationBundle.entry[coverage] 0..1 only when 'yes'. Seed bundle Patient-1 (Schmidt, carpenter) demonstrates WCBPOL (BG BAU). See ADR-0131.

Question: Q2
Notes: Six measurement axes, not four. Flexion/Abduction/at-side-ER stay LOINC valueQuantity degrees (41389-8/41381-5/41387-2). At-side Internal Rotation is a local valueCodeableConcept 8-tier vertebral-level ordinal ("hand behind back") rather than a degree measurement — goniometric IR degrees are clinically unreliable at this position (scapulothoracic substitution); the ordinal reuses most of Constant-Murley's own IR landmarks and adds finer rungs, so deriving the Constant ROM sub-score applies a documented lossy remapping. Two local degree axes — ER and IR measured at 90° abduction, an out-of-consensus enrichment — assess capsular tightness/GIRD and rotator-cuff competence that at-side measurement alone cannot quantify. All six rotation axes, active and passive, carry a 0–360° bound: permissive for data entry, not a claim that 360° is physiologically achievable. Flexion and Abduction stay bounded at 180°. Shared with Q12.d (ROM component). See ADR-0045, ADR-0088.
IG Implementation: LOINC 41389-8/41381-5/41387-2 on ShoulderFlexionObservation/ShoulderAbductionObservation/ShoulderExternalRotationObservation (valueQuantity deg, max 360 on ER); local #internal-rotation on ShoulderInternalRotationObservation (valueCodeableConcept, InternalRotationVertebralLevel required); local #external-rotation-90-abduction / #internal-rotation-90-abduction on new ShoulderExternalRotation90AbductionObservation / ShoulderInternalRotation90AbductionObservation (valueQuantity deg, max 360)

Question: Q2
Notes: Five measurement axes, not three. Manual muscle testing (0-5 ordinal, Janda grading — equivalent to MRC/Daniels-Worthingham) covers supraspinatus (Jobe position) / external-rotation composite (infraspinatus + teres minor) / subscapularis (lift-off or belly-press isolation) / internal-rotation composite (the mirror position of external-rotation, distinct from subscapularis isolation testing; ADR-0089). The supraspinatus ordinal + dynamometry pair is surfaced to clinicians as 'Abduction Strength', the Jobe/empty-can test position being a scapular-plane abduction — a display label only; profile and code identifiers are unaffected. See ADR-0107.
IG Implementation: #supraspinatus-strength / #external-rotation-strength / #subscapularis-strength / #internal-rotation-strength in ShoulderObservationCodes (valueQuantity MMT 0-5 each); #supraspinatus-strength-dynamometry (valueQuantity kg, max 50). Data Element: Radiographs in all patients with suspected RC tear

The registry-capturable fact is that a radiograph was obtained, recorded as a ShoulderImagingStudy with DICOM DX ("Digital Radiography") modality; the consensus names no radiology report object, so none is produced. Question: Q5
Data Element: Advanced imaging (MRI or CT) when planning/considering surgery
Notes: A5 is a clinical-timing/indication guideline ("when" to image), not a "capture this field" instruction (verified against Hurley et al. 2024; ADR-0130). Its substance is captured two ways at the same registration encounter: the advanced-modality ShoulderImagingStudy (MR/CT) that was obtained, and the imaging-derived classification Observations — gradings (Patte/Goutallier/Cofield tear-size) linked via Condition.stage.assessment, diagnostic evidence (tendons-involved, tear location, tear thickness) via Condition.evidence.detail (ADR-0073) — a participant cannot have those without advanced imaging having occurred. No imaging order (ServiceRequest) or radiology report (DiagnosticReport) object is required or produced (ADR-0172)
